back_translation: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends! Drink — drink your fill of love!

I was asleep, but my heart was awake. Listen! My beloved is knocking: “Open to me, my sister, my darling, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair wet with the droplets of the night.”
I have taken off my robe — must I put it on again? I have washed my feet — must I dirty them again?
My beloved put his hand in through the opening of the door, and my heart burned for him.
I rose to open for my beloved; my hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers wet with liquid myrrh, upon the bolt of the door.
I opened for my beloved, but my beloved had turned away and gone. My heart nearly broke when he departed. I sought him but did not find him; I called him but he did not answer.
The watchmen making their rounds of the city found me. They beat me and wounded me; the watchmen of the walls tore my cloak away from me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I make you swear: if you find my beloved, tell him that I am sick with love.
How is your beloved better than anyone else's beloved, O most beautiful among women? How is your beloved better than another's, that you make us swear like this?
My beloved is radiant and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
His head is like the purest gold; his hair is wavy in curls, black as a raven.
His eyes are like doves beside streams of water, bathed in milk and set like jewels.
His cheeks are like beds of spices sending out fragrance; his lips are like lilies dripping liquid myrrh.
His arms are like rounded gold set with beryl; his body is like polished ivory adorned with sapphires.
His legs are like pillars of marble set on bases of pure gold; his appearance is like Lebanon, majestic as the cedars.
His mouth is utter sweetness; all of him is altogether desirable. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
